title: Udyoga: the embassy, Krishna's counsel, Karna and Kunti
hook: Krishna speaks for peace before the whole Kuru court, Duryodhana walks out, and a plan to seize the envoy ends in a laugh
carry: no one could say it was never offered

segments.voice: Yesterday: Krishna carried Draupadi's words to Hastinapura, turned down a feast, and ate at Vidura's table. Your line was out of love, or out of need.

Morning in the great hall of the Kurus. Every seat is filled: Dhritarashtra on his throne, Bhishma, Drona, Vidura, Duryodhana and his brothers, Karna beside them. Krishna walks in, and the hall goes quiet. This is the moment the whole Udyoga has been building toward: a formal chance to stop the war, spoken face to face, in front of everyone who matters.
screen: `THE HALL IS FULL.` → `KRISHNA WALKS IN.` → `A CHANCE TO STOP THE WAR.`

segments.voice: Krishna speaks to Dhritarashtra first, and his argument is simple. You can stop this. Your sons and your nephews could stand together, and no one could stand against them. Peace would be your gain, not your loss. Give the Pandavas their share. Others speak after him. Old sages tell stories of pride brought low. Bhishma and Drona urge Duryodhana to make peace. Duryodhana hears them, and refuses. He says, in effect, that he won't give the Pandavas even as much land as the point of a needle would cover, and he walks out of the hall. Then Gandhari, his mother, is sent for. He is called back to hear her, and she tells her son plainly that a person who can't rule his own anger and greed can't rule a kingdom. He leaves again. Outside, he and his friends make a plan: seize Krishna, tie him up, and the Pandavas will be helpless. Word reaches the hall. And Krishna laughs. The text says that as he laughed, his body blazed, and gods and heroes seemed to stream out of him, so bright the court had to shut their eyes. Only a few could look: Bhishma, Drona, Vidura and the sages, and Dhritarashtra, granted sight for that moment. Then the vision ends, and Krishna walks calmly out. The point isn't only the wonder. Krishna came anyway. The night before, at Vidura's, he said he had come so that no one could blame him for not trying. So he made the whole case for peace in public, where no one could say it was never offered.
screen: `KRISHNA: PEACE IS YOUR GAIN` · `NOT EVEN A NEEDLE'S POINT OF LAND` · `GANDHARI: RULE YOUR OWN ANGER` · then, large: `A PLOT, A LAUGH, A BLAZING FORM`

segments.voice: Krishna made his case for peace even though he expected a no; bring to mind one good thing you've been holding back from saying because you think it won't be heard. Breathing in, say it silently, all the way through, and breathing out, let go of needing a yes, since you've offered it, at least to yourself. If you pray, you can offer it in your prayer as well.
Udyoga. The getting ready, where Krishna makes the case for peace in front of the whole Kuru court, and Duryodhana refuses.
Your line: no one could say it was never offered. The peace was spoken aloud, in front of everyone. That's day eight hundred sixteen.

howItsDone: Krishna's embassy to the Kuru court is retold in Hindu storytelling and performance, and the form he reveals in the assembly is heard by some readers as a glimpse of the vision later shown to Arjuna.

laugh, and let the court see who you are.

original.note: effort, getting ready; the embassy in the assembly is a public effort for peace.

chat.says: If Krishna expected Duryodhana to refuse, why did he bother making the case for peace?
options: So no one could say peace was never offered; he made the whole case in public.
He hoped to trick the court into a trap so the Pandavas could attack first.
He believed Duryodhana would surely agree once Bhishma spoke first.
chat.meaning: Krishna told Vidura he came so no one could blame him for not trying. He made the whole case for peace in front of the court.

Gandhari.meaning: Duryodhana's mother, who tells him to rule his own anger

Karna.meaning: a great warrior on Duryodhana's side

Duryodhana.meaning: eldest of the Kauravas, the Pandavas' rival cousin

Dhritarashtra.meaning: the blind Kuru king, father of Duryodhana

Udyoga.meaning: effort, getting ready; the book of the epic before the war
